item.title: Visa period to Australia to be made longer for businesspeople and simplified processes expected for those who have previously held an Australian visa
item.description: Some good news as Fijians who wish to travel to Australia may have a longer stay, easier and flexible visa after the implementation of the Vuvale Union which is expected to make travel between the two countries easier. This was highlighted by the Australian High Commissioner to Fiji, Peter Roberts during the fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan when questioned on Fijians calling for visa f
item.content:encoded:
Some good news as Fijians who wish to travel to Australia may have a longer stay, easier and flexible visa after the implementation of the Vuvale Union which is expected to make travel between the two countries easier.

This was highlighted by the Australian High Commissioner to Fiji, Peter Roberts during the fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan when questioned on Fijians calling for visa free travel to Australia for years.

The High Commissioner says Australia has a universal visa system whereby anyone who travels to Australia must have a visa.

However, Roberts says under the Vuvale Union, regulatory changes will be made to extend the time that people are able to stay on a visitor visa, especially for business visas.

He says business travellers will also have the opportunity to apply for multiple-entry visas valid for up to five years.

He says they will also be working to simplify the visa application processes, particularly for people who have previously held an Australian visa and applicants may no longer have to repeatedly provide the same information each time they apply.

The High Commissioner says this will also allow Fijians to travel to Australia and return to Fiji more easily and for longer periods, while also encouraging more Australians to visit Fiji, invest and bring their skills to the country.

item.title: Raised with Love, now giving love: Youth pastor Nancy Cakacaka shares her story on fijivillage HerStory at 7pm Wednesday
item.description: Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation. Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.
item.content:encoded:
Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation.

Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.

On this week’s fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, Nancy opens up about her own journey, from growing up in Bua with her grandparents after her parents separated, to the values of love, faith and discipline that shaped her upbringing.

She also shares her experiences working with young people, the challenges families and youths face today, and her message to young people to listen to their parents, stay grounded in their faith and know that they are loved.

Join us at 7pm Wednesday for fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, as we hear Aunty Nancy's story.

item.title: Family shaken after alleged robbery at their home
item.description: Sandeep Prakash told fijivillage News that his family members were awake at the time and a man was waiting in their backyard. Prakash says no one was injured during the incident, but clothes and food items were stolen.
item.content:encoded:
Sandeep Prakash told fijivillage News that his family members were awake at the time and a man was waiting in their backyard.

Prakash says no one was injured during the incident, but clothes and food items were stolen.

He says the matter was reported to the Nausori Police Station last night.

Prakash says while the family is shocked and frightened by what happened, they are thankful that everyone is safe.

He says the safety and well-being of his family are more important than anything else and is urging people to remain alert, look after their families and keep their homes secure.

item.title: 51 years later former Hibiscus Queen hopes to reunite with her 1975 Miss Charity
item.description: More than five decades after they stood together under the spotlight at Albert Park, former Hibiscus Queen Michele Smith is hoping to find the woman who shared one of the most memorable nights of her life. In 1975, 19-year-old Letila Vaukatagane was crowned Miss Charity, while Smith was crowned Hibiscus Queen.
item.content:encoded:
More than five decades after they stood together under the spotlight at Albert Park, former Hibiscus Queen Michele Smith is hoping to find the woman who shared one of the most memorable nights of her life.

In 1975, 19-year-old Letila Vaukatagane was crowned Miss Charity, while Smith was crowned Hibiscus Queen.

Smith went on to travel, fulfilling one of the dreams however, 51 years later she is wondering what became of Letila.

Smith is now in Suva volunteering for the FMF Hibiscus Festival 2026 and is hoping the festival can help bring the two former queens together again.

She says the Hibiscus Queen may receive much of the attention, but the Miss Charity contestants are the ones who quietly work behind the scenes, alongside their families and friends, to raise funds for the festival.

Smith says these women are often the unsung heroines of the Hibiscus Festival and deserve to be remembered for the work they did.

She says reconnecting with Letila would be special and hopes they can sit down together, share memories and perhaps even do an interview for old times’ sake.

Festival Director Ellen Whippy-Knight says while many people can remember their favourite Hibiscus Queen, it is often difficult to name former Miss Charity queens.

She says the festival wants to recognise the women who have contributed to its long history through fundraising and service.

The Miss Charity tradition remains an important part of the Hibiscus Festival, with contestants this year once again carrying out fundraising initiatives aimed at supporting communities and people in need.

The 2026 contestants are involved in activities ranging from community outreach and health awareness to grassroots campaigns.

As the festival celebrates its legacy, Smith's search is a reminder of the stories and friendships that can sometimes be left behind when the pageant lights go out.

For Smith, finding Letila is about more than reconnecting with a fellow contestant from 1975.

It is about remembering a young woman who stood beside her that night and making sure her contribution to the Hibiscus Festival is not forgotten.

She is now hoping that Letila Vaukatagane will see the call and get in touch the festival is looking for Letila.
